description: Run a script on Linux instance to perform memory acquisition

limePath.description: (Optional) Path to the LiME Kernel module on disk. If not provided, LiME will be downloaded and built

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# RHEL memory acquisition. This runs on the instance under investigation.
# AVML is used as a prebuilt static binary rather than compiled here. The
# previous revision installed a third party yum repository, downloaded musl
# RPMs from forensics.cert.org, compiled musl 1.2.2 from source, installed a
# Rust toolchain from rustup.rs and then had cargo vendor and compile OpenSSL
# for the musl target - all on the instance under investigation, during an
# incident. On a current RHEL 8.10 AMI that build does not complete: it needs
# gcc for cargo's host build scripts and Perl modules RHEL 8 does not ship for
# OpenSSL's ./Configure, and even with both it fails later in the OpenSSL
# compile. AVML publishes a statically linked x86_64 binary per release, which
# is what the build was trying to produce.
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
kernel_release=$(uname -r)
kernel_name=$(uname -s)
# RHEL 8 has no awscli package at all - `yum list --available awscli` returns
# "No matching Packages" - and the previous `pip3 install awscli` left nothing
# on root's PATH, so every aws call failed with "command not found" while the
# script carried on. Install AWS CLI v2 from the official archive.
if ! command -v aws >/dev/null 2>&1; then
sudo yum install -yq unzip curl || fail 'cannot install unzip'
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip || fail 'cannot download the AWS CLI'
( cd /tmp && unzip -q -o awscliv2.zip && sudo ./aws/install --update ) || fail 'cannot install the AWS CLI'
export PATH=/usr/local/bin:$PATH
fi
command -v aws >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'the AWS CLI is not available, so the capture could not be uploaded'
# Why AWS credentials arrive as document parameters rather than an instance role:
# these are short-lived STS session credentials, minted per acquisition by the
# forensic Lambda with a session policy scoped to this case's S3 prefix - not
# long-lived IAM access keys. The host this runs on cannot be given an instance
# profile for the evidence bucket: it is either the machine under investigation,
# whose configuration must not be changed mid-incident, or an analysis host that
# must not hold standing access to other cases' evidence. Do not copy this
# pattern into a workload where an IAM role is available.
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
sudo rm -rf /tmp/forensic_tools && mkdir -p /tmp/forensic_tools
cd /tmp/forensic_tools || fail 'cannot create the tool directory'
# Prefer a copy staged in the evidence bucket, exactly as the Linux document
# does for its LiME modules, so an instance with no route to GitHub can still
# be imaged. Fall back to the pinned upstream release.
AVML_VERSION=v0.20.0
avml_path=
if aws s3 cp "s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/avml/avml" ./avml && [ -s ./avml ]; then
avml_path=$(pwd)/avml
echo "using the AVML binary staged at s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/avml/avml"
else
curl -fsSL -o ./avml "https://github.com/microsoft/avml/releases/download/${AVML_VERSION}/avml" || fail "cannot download AVML ${AVML_VERSION}"
[ -s ./avml ] || fail "the downloaded AVML ${AVML_VERSION} binary is empty"
avml_path=$(pwd)/avml
echo "using AVML ${AVML_VERSION} downloaded from the upstream release"
fi
chmod +x "$avml_path" || fail 'cannot make the AVML binary executable'
# AVML is statically linked, so this also proves the binary runs on this host
# before it is trusted with the acquisition.
"$avml_path" --version || fail 'the AVML binary will not execute on this host'
# `avml <file>` was the AVML 0.x CLI. Current releases take a subcommand and
# reject a bare path with "unrecognized subcommand", which produced no capture
# while the old script reported success.
sudo "$avml_path" acquire output.lime
# Refuse to publish a capture that was never taken. avml failing left no
# output.lime, and the script still uploaded a zero byte lime_sha256.txt and
# exited 0, so the case recorded a successful memory acquisition.
if [ ! -s output.lime ] ; then
echo "MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: avml produced no memory capture for $kernel_release" >&2
exit 1
fi
echo copying...to {{s3ArtifactLocation}}/$kernel_release.lime
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
MEMSIZE=`awk '/MemTotal/ {print $2/1024/1024}' /proc/meminfo`
S3_EXPECTED_SIZE=`awk '/MemTotal/ {print $2*1024}' /proc/meminfo`
ACL_FLAG="--acl bucket-owner-full-control"
METADATA_FLAG="--metadata uncompressed-size=$MEMSIZE,kernel-name=$kernel_name,kernel-release=$kernel_release"
EXPECTED_SIZE_FLAG="--expected-size $S3_EXPECTED_SIZE"
aws s3 cp output.lime {{s3ArtifactLocation}}/ $EXPECTED_SIZE_FLAG $METADATA_FLAG $ACL_FLAG || { echo 'MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: s3 upload of the memory capture failed' >&2; exit 1; }
sha256sum output.lime > lime_sha256.txt || { echo 'MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: cannot hash the memory capture' >&2; exit 1; }
aws s3 cp lime_sha256.txt {{s3ArtifactLocation}}/ $ACL_FLAG || { echo 'MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: s3 upload of the capture hash failed' >&2; exit 1; }
exit 0;
